ops.title: cc-pool is not a repin: 4 no-successor subsystems + live proc.Record SQL keys
ops.body:
S3.b recon verdict (2026-08-03). cc-pool at origin/main 8df819e cannot be migrated to daemonkit v0.21 as a repin. Measured with an alias-resolved import scan over 91 daemonkit-importing and 36 fusekit-importing Go files.

FOUR SUBSYSTEMS WITH NO v0.21 SUCCESSOR

1. Process-record ledger (52 files, 24 non-test / 28 test). cc-pool uses proc.Record(78), FileStore(37), Reaper(27), OwnerGeneration(23), ReapReceipt(14), ProcessGeneration(13), ReapReceiptCursor(7), RecoveryID, RecordDigest, ErrReceiptBacklog. v0.21 offers only Owned.Reclaimed() -> Reclaimed{PID,Exit}. No durable, paged, acknowledgeable reap-receipt feed.

2. worker.Pool (32 files, 15 non-test / 17 test). Guide says no successor. Only 2 real construction sites (internal/pool/workers.go:93 with Capacity 4 / QueueCapacity 4 / MaxTotalRun 31m / 16MiB stdio caps; scripts/vm/helpers/worker-deadline/main.go:56); the other 30 pass CommandRequest/CommandResult as plain values through the cc-pool-local workerexec.Runner interface.

3. daemonkit/wire runtime + observation lane (24 files). internal/daemon/transport.go:53-96 runs its own wire.Server + wire.NewRuntime + wire.ObservationRoute; internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:99 returns wire.StreamResponse. Streaming and server-pushed events are withdrawn with no successor. internal/daemon/wirebuildgen has a CI -check drift gate on the generated wire identity.

4. trust 3-role model (19 files): trust.PeerRole(27), VerifierWorkerBudgets, RunVerifierChild, NewTrustPolicy, ProcessVerifier, UnprotectedRole -> v0.21 Requirement/Serving/Trust/Caller.

THE BLOCKING ONE IS LIVE DATA, NOT COMPILE ERRORS

proc.Record is json.Marshal'd (internal/store/credential_operation.go:2707) into owner_record BLOB columns of three SQLite tables (credential_operations, account_mutations, pending_adds) and used as a SQL EQUALITY KEY alongside owner_epoch: WHERE token=? AND owner_record=? AND owner_epoch=? (credential_operation.go:832,1054,1114,1199,1744; reserve.go:70,89,339). Takeover bumps owner_epoch only after verifying a daemonkit ReapReceipt (credential_operation.go:1139-1160, pool/credential_recovery.go:96-205). This fences credential-refresh and account-mutation sagas against two owners. proc.Record is a 9-field json-tagged struct (daemonkit@v0.20.9/proc/reaper.go:58). Any change to that encoding silently orphans in-flight sagas on real user machines at upgrade rather than resuming them.

SUBSTRATES ARE READY (not the blocker)
- daemonkit v0.21.3 tagged; fusekit v1.16.0 NOT yet tagged (worktree /private/tmp/w1-fusekit has trustroles deleted and holder.Config free of *proc.FileStore).
- synckit v0.37.1 tagged. THIRD LOCKSTEP PIN THE BRIEF OMITTED: cc-pool pins synckit v0.35.2, whose helperruntime.Config takes *worker.Pool/*proc.Manager/*proc.FileStore by field type. v0.37.0 dropped them: Config{App, Program, Dispatcher, MaxFrame, Prepare func(daemonkit.Ctx)}.

BRIEF CORRECTIONS
- The pin gate is .github/scripts/verify-suite-pins.sh (not scripts/), with a sibling verify-suite-pins_test.sh. It checks daemonkit + fusekit go.mod versions against widget/project.yml Swift exactVersion pins (currently FuseKit 1.15.5 / DaemonKit 0.20.9), so the Swift pins bump too. It does NOT cover synckit.
- CI needs almost nothing: ci.yml already has a macos-15 test job through scripts/test.sh (a ulimit -u harness), GOOS=darwin lint+vuln on ubuntu, and the CGO_ENABLED=1 runtime-archive build. Only PR-only cancel-in-progress concurrency is missing.
- Trap 4 pre-solved: internal/testhome sets DAEMONKIT_HOME as well as HOME.
- Self-exec TestMains confirmed in internal/daemon, internal/hostsync, internal/cli, cmd/cc-pool; internal/pool/workers.go:109 really re-execs the .test binary as a disposable worker. Harness mandatory.

RECOMMENDATION: design-first, same treatment fusekit's F1 got. The cheapest safe answer is probably lifting daemonkit v0.20.9's proc package verbatim into cc-pool internal/ to freeze the JSON encoding, but permanently forking ~2000 lines of process supervision into a consumer is an orchestrator call, not a lane call.
